subject: Pilot economics — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@blueriverpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics — post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks for the 30m today. Quick recap of the problems you shared, goals, and a simple pilot suggestion so we can validate ROI quickly.

Pain points and goals:
- Production latency spikes on inference during peak hours causing checkout friction (~180-250ms average now, target <100ms).
- Token-heavy receipts and personalization flows driving high spend (~1.8M tokens/day on average per model).
- Goal: reduce per-conversation unit cost by 40–60% while keeping >95% of current quality.

Initial economics framing:
- Your current unit cost (third-party endpoint) ~ $0.0025/token.
- With batching + prefix/KV cache and quantized model candidate we project ~$0.0007–$0.0010/token in pilot conditions (see attached estimate).

Recommended pilot (1 month):
- Scope: 2M tokens/day, inference for receipts + personalization (subset of traffic, 10% sample).
- Config: Redwood hosted with quantized v1-small model variant, 8-request batching window (~40–60ms additional latency), prefix cache for repeat user histories.
- Success metrics: unit cost <= $0.0010/token, P99 latency <200ms for sample, minimal quality regressions on 5 eval prompts.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-estimate.pdf and a short mutual action plan link below. Next steps:
1) Ben to share a tighter per-token estimate and technical checklist (cc'd).
2) Alex to confirm pilot scope and any compliance requirements by EOD Tue.
3) We'll schedule a 20m handoff with CS for onboarding once terms match.

Thanks — Jasmine
--

Alex — following up with the numbers you asked for. Attached: batching-savings-model.xlsx with sensitivity table.

Quick highlights (assumes same model quality):
- 1M tokens/day -> estimated $0.0011/token (with conservative cache hit 12%, batching factor 3).
- 2M tokens/day -> estimated $0.00078/token (cache hit 18%, batching factor 5).
- 3M tokens/day -> estimated $0.00066/token (cache hit 22%, batching factor 6).

Assumptions: avg prompt+response = 1,200 tokens, 60% of requests share prefixes eligible for cache. Ops notes:
- We can keep P95 latency <120ms with the batching window set to 30–60ms; P99 will be workload dependent but we saw ~180–220ms in similar customers.
- Retention: by default we support customer-managed retention settings; SOC2 artifacts are in the security packet (I'll put a short summary in the MAP).

Attachments: batching-savings-model.xlsx

If you want, we can run a simulated 48-hr replay on a 10% sample of your logs to refine estimates before committing.
